geometry_source: Harvard CHGIS Japan Tokugawa GIS 2004, jp_toku_kuni_pgn.shp (DOI 10.7910/DVN/2CVTR0) compared to artifacts/data/population_capacity/location_geometry_calibrated.parquet

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Buzen no kuni polygon from the Harvard CHGIS Tokugawa Japan GIS 2004 dataset; used as a documented approximation to the medieval Buzen province in Farris Table 1.3.

area_comparison.historical_polygon_source: Harvard CHGIS jp_toku_kuni_pgn.shp, Buzen no kuni

crosswalks.resolution_method: Downloaded the Harvard CHGIS historical-province polygon and checked all three EU5 Buzen calibrated centroids against it. All three centroids are inside the historical polygon; the EU5 union area exceeds the historical polygon by 4.35%. The declared 0.96 coverage is a conservative contract accounting for the coarse EU5 location footprint and the 1828-versus-1280 boundary date gap. No name-only mapping is used.
crosswalks.notes: Lower-bound use tolerates a small containing-area overhang: the model must support at least the recorded Buzen floor over the selected EU5 footprint. This crosswalk must not be interpreted as a two-sided province-capacity label.

crosswalks.historical_boundary: Noto no kuni polygon from the Harvard CHGIS Tokugawa Japan GIS 2004 dataset; used as a documented approximation to the medieval Noto province in Farris Table 1.3.

area_comparison.historical_polygon_source: Harvard CHGIS jp_toku_kuni_pgn.shp, Noto no kuni

crosswalks.resolution_method: Downloaded the Harvard CHGIS historical-province polygon and checked all three EU5 Noto centroids against it. All three centroids are inside the historical polygon; the EU5 union area exceeds the historical polygon by 5.23%. The declared 0.95 coverage is deliberately conservative and accounts for the coarse EU5 footprint and the 1828-versus-1280 boundary date gap.
crosswalks.notes: Farris's possible omitted-paddy problem makes the retained value a conservative floor. The crosswalk is not a claim that the low observed Noto population was the intrinsic capacity.
